tools.name: match_procedure
tools.description: Cosine-matches procedural memory (curated 'how to' patterns the operator recorded) against a free-text context query. Returns top-K procedures sorted by similarity DESC then priority ASC. Surfaces the behaviour rules that apply to a context — e.g. "user asks about pricing" → "mention they're on plat

tools.name: list_procedures
tools.description: Paginated listing of procedural memory for admin/review UIs. Sorted by priority ASC, createdAt DESC. Set includeRetired=true to see soft-deleted rows.

tools.name: search_communities
tools.description: Cosine-matches the query against topic-community summaries — the coarse retrieval scope. A community is a cluster of related entities (label propagation over the entity graph) with one rolled-up summary. Suited to broad questions ("what do we know about X domain"): it returns an overview of a domain

tools.name: list_communities
tools.description: Paginated listing of topic communities, largest first. Each row carries a label, a rolled-up summary, and the member count. Gives the knowledge map at a glance.

tools.name: find_entity_communities
tools.description: Returns the topic communities a given entity is a member of. Places an entity in its broader context — which clusters / themes it participates in — and leads from one entity to the wider neighbourhood the cluster summarises.

tools.name: why
tools.description: Return the design decisions, rationale, invariants and gotchas recorded against a code anchor — the non-derivable engineering "why" a parser cannot recover from source. tools.name: recall_decisions
tools.description: Find recorded design decisions / rationale / invariants / gotchas by NL topic ("why do we resolve facts through one gateway?"), across ALL code anchors — a semantic search over code-memory, rather than one known anchor. Returns matches with their code anchor + kind, ranked by relevance.

tools.description: Return everything brain knows ABOUT a source (not its facts): the operator-declared identity (type, authLevel — authority in conflict resolution), the learned per-domain agreement rates (domain = predicate; null domain = the global blended rate; rates need >=8 samples before the resolver trusts them

tools.description: The tenant this credential writes to (companyId, its display name, whether it is a personal workspace), what is already in its memory (entities, active facts, facts recorded in the last 7 days), how many Domain Packs are installed, for a user-bound connection who the user is in this memory (`user.na

tools.name: record_fact
tools.description: Insert a fact about an entity. Triggers brain conflict resolution (INSERTED / SUPERSEDED / COMPETING / REJECTED). Most facts come from event ingestion; this records one directly.

tools.name: link_entities
tools.description: Insert an edge between two entities. `kind` is the edge type — `identity_of` merges the `from` entity into `to` (cross-vertical identity reconciliation), other typed edges (`paid_for`, `mentioned_in`, `worked_with`, …) are surfaced in related-entity reads and contribute to PPR / SubgraphRAG context.

tools.name: retract_fact
tools.description: Mark a fact as no longer believed. Cascades to facts derived from this one. Does not delete; the row remains for audit.

tools.name: record_procedure

tools.name: retire_procedure
tools.description: Mark a procedural memory row as retired (sets retiredAt). A retired procedure is no longer matched or listed by default. For a rule that no longer applies — distinct from a hard delete because the row stays for audit.

tools.name: record_decision

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: synthesize, get_competing_facts, list_procedures · Private data: detect_contradiction, get_fact, why, workspace_status, record_fact, record_procedure, record_decision · Public sink: record_procedure · Destructive: detect_contradiction, search_communities, retract_fact, retire_procedure.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: synthesize, get_competing_facts, list_procedures · Private data: detect_contradiction, get_fact, why, workspace_status, record_fact, record_procedure, record_decision · Public sink: record_procedure · Destructive: detect_contradiction, search_communities, retract_fact, retire_procedure

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
